title: Capsule Review: examination-separated blood-CNN sampling comparison
status: Frozen before new optimisation. Earlier data labels, exploratory examination transfer outcomes, original pilot and Galar23 negative results have already been inspected. All outcomes remain exploratory, not blinded or patient-independent.
question: When fitting from scratch on exactly the same 14 permitted Galar fitting examinations, does examination/class-balanced sampling with predetermined moderate photometric jitter improve within-held-out-examination blood-label ranking over matched-update pooled cross-entropy training?

source.Galar: Le Floch et al. corrected Galar v2; CC BY 4.0

known_support.original_training_1_to_8: 4096 images; 239 blood-positive images across five exams; 3/5/8 are blood-negative-labelled
known_support.fitting_21_23_25_27_29_30: 6027 original PNGs, 1424 explicit blood-positive annotations, intentionally enriched selection in each new source exam
known_support.all: 10123 unique source PNGs; 1663 explicit blood-positive labels; every original image hash and source identity verified before fitting

source.allowed_images: Original 1-8 fixed 512 snapshots plus the 6 verified exam-level unions. Per-fold fit uses all fitting rows ONLY outside its held-out exam IDs, and evaluation only each held-out exam's 512 uniform label-blind reference positions. Never evaluate on enriched-only rows.
source.prohibited: Never read source exams 9-10 (historical checkpoint selection) or reserved 11-20 or authors' 61-80. Do not use original CNN checkpoint as initial weight, since it was trained on old studies included as held-out validation here. No unverified patient independence.

model.architecture: existing capsule_review.baseline.AnatomyCNN(2), random initialization from a common seed separately in each fold and arm
model.preprocessing: Existing original PIL EXIF transpose + ImageOps.pad to 96x96 black-padded RGB then float32 [0,1]; no source-label-guided crop
model.device: float32 CPU, fixed 2 torch threads, torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
model.checkpoint: Final optimizer update only, no epoch/checkpoint tuning, exactly 3 folds * 2 arms = 6 trained models

arms.name: pooled_weighted
arms.sampling: Sample uniformly with replacement across all permitted fit images using fixed seeded RNG
arms.loss: Cross entropy, train-pool inverse-frequency class weights, normalised so average weight about 1, no cap; no augmentation

arms.name: exam_balanced_jitter
arms.sampling: Sample exam uniformly with replacement across the fit exam IDs, then sample class with probability 0.5 when both explicit classes present in that exam; if only one class present, use that class. Sample an original image uniformly from that exam/class
arms.loss: Unweighted cross entropy, balancing is only in sampling
arms.preprocessing_change: Fixed train-only brightness multiplier independently uniform [0.75,1.25] and saturation multiplier [0.75,1.25], clamp to [0,1], black padding remains black; no validation augmentation

reporting.primary: Per-examination ROC-AUC on label-blind 512-reference images for positive-containing exams with >=10 positive reference labels; macro-average, every exam reported regardless of support
reporting.secondary: Per-exam AP, ROC-AUC also when 1-9 positives (highly unstable), exactly K=51/128/256/512 top-K blood-positive image hits and corresponding uniform comparator, precision at K (descriptive only), blood-negative examinations 3/5/8 reported with ROC-AUC undefined and uncalibrated score distribution
reporting.abstention: Every arm picks K per exam in top-K comparisons; 100% 512 ceiling, no clinical sensitivity or physician reading-time claim
reporting.uncertainty: No frame-wise inferential CI/p-values. Small exam count and unknown patient independence; macro statistics descriptive only.
reporting.model_selection: Retain both candidates and historical failures regardless of scores; do not promote any model on these previously examined fitting studies. No tuning after results.
reporting.sources: Only aggregate public per-exam results and source digests in Git; private scores, image IDs, weights and per-image labels in Capsule Review Library.
